'''Mohammad Basil Altaie''' (also known as '''Mohammed Bassel al-Tai''', born March 5, 1952) is an [[Iraq|Iraqi]] physicist, philosopher and professor of [[theoretical physics]] at [[Yarmouk University]] in [[Jordan]].<ref name="The Muslim 500">{{cite web |title=Dr Basil Altaie |url=https://themuslim500.com/book-reviews-2020/the-divine-word-and-the-grand-design/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231210062212/https://www.themuslim500.com/book-reviews-2020/the-divine-word-and-the-grand-design/ |archive-date=2023-12-10 |access-date=2021-12-27 |website=The Muslim 500}}</ref><ref name="Faculty Websites 2021">{{cite web |date=2021-12-27 |title=Dr. Mohammed. B. Altaie |url=https://faculty.yu.edu.jo/maltaie/SitePages/About%20Me.aspx |url-status=dead |access-date=2021-12-27 |website=Faculty Websites |archive-date=2021-12-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211227131804/https://faculty.yu.edu.jo/maltaie/SitePages/About%20Me.aspx }}</ref>

==Biography==
Muhammad Basil Altaie was born on March 5, 1952, in [[Mosul|Mosul, Iraq]], where he completed his primary and secondary education.{{sfn|الخلاوي|2018|p=294}}{{sfn|Daneshgar|Saleh|2016|p=348}} In 1970, he enrolled at the [[University of Mosul]] to study [[physics]], a subject that had captivated him since high school. During his studies in 1972, Altaie authored a book on general and special relativity, which he submitted to the rector of the [[University of Baghdad]]. The rector sent the book to a scientific reviewer, Dr. Sami Hassan al-Samarrai, who approved it without knowing that Altaie was still a student.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2021-08-28 |title=Seminar on the cosmologist Dr. Mohammed Basel al-Taie |url=https://en.uobaghdad.edu.iq/?p=28757 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240709001303/https://en.uobaghdad.edu.iq/?p=28757 |archive-date=2024-07-09 |access-date=2024-07-09 |website=University of Baghdad |language=en-US}}</ref>

Following his graduation from the University of Mosul in June 1974, the Iraqi government awarded Altaie a scholarship to pursue a doctorate in theoretical physics. He enrolled at the [[University of Manchester]] in the United Kingdom the same year and received his Ph.D. in theoretical physics in 1978.<ref name="KRM">{{cite web |title=KRM: Staff: Scholars |url=https://www.kalamresearch.com/staff.php?category=2&staffid=79 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211227140016/https://www.kalamresearch.com/staff.php?category=2&staffid=79 |archive-date=2021-12-27 |access-date=2021-12-27 |website=KRM}}</ref>

After returning to his country, Iraq, Altae worked at the University of Mosul, where he remained until 1999. Since 1999, he has worked as an assistant professor of physics at [[Yarmouk University]] in [[Jordan]], where he was promoted to the rank of professor in 2003. He has been identified as a member of a "new generation of authors" interested in the debate over [[Islamic attitudes towards science|Islam and science]], with [[Mehdi Golshani]], [[Bruno Guiderdoni]], and [[Nidhal Guessoum]], who, as [[Natural science|natural scientists]], seek a [[Theistic science|theistic interpretation of science]] based on [[Science in the medieval Islamic world|Islamic concepts]].{{sfn | Daneshgar | Saleh | 2016 | p=348}}

==Views==
Altaie argues that [[quantum indeterminacy]] provides credibility to Islamic theism. The universe, according to Altaie, is both extremely [[Predictability|predictable]] and [[Indeterminism|indeterministic]]. It is predictable, which is why "[[Scientific law|laws of nature]]" exist, yet it is indeterministic, indicating that these laws are not absolute. The order of nature, he believes, is evidence of Divine wisdom, and its unpredictability, he believes, is a symbol of continuous creation.{{sfn | Yazicioglu |2021| p=276-277}}

==Works==
* ''The Divine Word and The Grand Design: Interpreting the Qur'an in the Light of Modern Science (2019)''
* ''God, Nature, and the Cause: Essays on Islam and Science (2016)''
